rationale: Round 1 compiled and passed, so the headroom exists to push control-flow obfuscation harder on this tiny 14-function benchmark dominated by the huge init function (~40KB text). FLA stays the strongest lever since flattening init's large switch-like search dispatch maximally resists static analysis, and BCF weights are raised (SecurityGain 0.75) to add opaque-predicate noise inside the hot search loops; SPLIT and IBR are kept elevated to fragment and randomize basic blocks, compounding the flattened dispatcher. SUB is held at moderate weights because Searching-flt is float-heavy ( Searching-flt kernels) and aggressive instruction substitution on FP code risks numerical drift for limited gain, while ICALL and IGV remain light: indirect-call and global-variable indirection add modest resistance at low size cost, but the program's small data footprint means heavier IGV would bloat without much payoff. All RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept in the 0.2-0.4 band since round 1 showed no runtime or size pressure yet, and CorrectnessRisk stays near or above 0.5 so the selector only applies transforms where feature confidence is high.
